description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Accuracy@1 on geometry problems and the number of child nodes, also referred to as tree width. The x-axis is labeled “Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)” and has a linear scale ranging from 1 to 7, with tick labels at each integer value. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy@1 (%)” and has a linear scale ranging from 15 to 35, with tick labels at intervals of 5.  A blue line, marked with circular data points and representing GPT-4o, begins at 24.4% at a tree width of 1 and declines to 31.1% at a tree width of 5, then decreases to 20.0% at a tree width of 7. A light blue line, marked with cross-shaped data points and representing Claude-3.5-Sonnet, begins at 26.7% at a tree width of 1 and increases to 27.8% at a tree width of 3, then rises to 34.4% at a tree width of 5, and finally decreases to 31.1% at a tree width of 7.
caption_used: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (RIGHT) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with GPT-4o peaking at 31.1% and Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforming GPT-4o across all tree widths.
